page.layout: One printed page, 172, with running head "DE MILITIA ROMANA" at the top. One text column, with marginal notes in the left margin beside the text. The facing page edge at the right of the scan is not transcribed.

main_text.p: fantes. Ubi Alam etiam dicit partem illam humeri bra-chiique adiutricem in hoc nisu. Quid, quòd ipsa incur-ua illa pars, Umbo? Fallor, aut sic Statius:Umbo pro humero.
De Tydeo ait, defesso à pugnâ & vix arma sustinente. Ibi Luctatius: Hic umbonem pro humero posuit, aut pro manu. Martialis consimiliter, de valente suo liberto:

p.i: In turbam incideris, cunctos umbone repellet.

main_text.p: Profectò ista pars brachij est, proiecta & incuruans. Sa-tis de Scuto, pro Polybij quidem mente. Aud. Non etiam pro mea. Lips. Quid abest, aut aues igitur? Aud. Principium & inductionem scuti, ob Liuij ver-ba (in mente habeo) quae me torquent. Nam cùm illa de {*}Ordine legebamus, haec quoque erant: Clypeis antea Romani usi sunt, deinde postquam stipendiarij facti sunt, scuta pro clypeis fecere. Ergone tunc demum scuta intro-ducta, cùm stipendia, id est obsidione Veienti? Atqui ipse Liuius aliter, & iam in armandis classibus Seruia-nis, dat primori dumtaxat clypeos (ἀσπίδας ἀργολικὰς [?] Dio-nysius:) reliquis scuta, quos Θυρεὸς idem ibi Graecus. Sed & saepius antea Scutorum mentio. Lips. Me spectas? prope est ut negem respondere ad talia quae abducunt extra Polybianum campum. Sed tamen quia in margi-ne haeres, fiat. {Tetigi}Liuij inte-rior sen-tentia. supra leuiter de sensu verborum Liuij, qui non est (ut verba aspecta praeferunt) quasi an-tea clypeis tantum Romani usi, postea scutis. Id vero falsum: sed quod utrumque genus in usu antea, postin-de sola scuta. Breuiter haec sententia. Origo igitur Scu-torum à regibus, imo à primo ipso rege, si fidem habes Plutarcho. Ille sic de Romulo: Θυρεοῖς τὴν Σαβίνων ὁ ῥω-μύλος [?]Romulus scuta in-duxit.In Romulo
* Lib. II. Dial. III. Lib. VII. Quando Romanis scuta.

page.notes: The text is in a dense, slightly worn Roman type with the printed u/v and i/j forms, which I have normalised. "Luctatius" is printed with a c-cedilla form and may be Lactatius; I left it as read. The Greek in the Dionysius and Plutarch passages is small and worn, so the accents and final letters are uncertain; those words are marked [?]. The "*" mark before "Ordine" and the note "* Lib. II. Dial. III. Lib. VII. Quando Romanis scuta." are linked by the asterisk; the note is placed as a footnote-style line because its position in the margin spans several lines. The Statius verse line has an ornamental mark before "Mutatum" that I did not transcribe. The "Lib. II." note and "Umbo pro humero." note are placed beside their lines as printed. No catchword or signature is visible.
